purpose: Bundled snapshot of stable public reference data (BLS/ONET wage tables, ACS metro housing stats, industry recruiting benchmarks) so scout does not re-fetch it live every run. Scout loads this file FIRST and spends its web budget only on role-specific facts this file cannot carry: named target companies, hiring triggers, live posting language, comp postings for the specific role being researched.
usage_note: Every figure here is Sourced from the named public series at the stated as_of vintage. When scout cites a value from this file in pack.json or pack-research.json, the method field names the original source and this file's as_of vintage (not today's date), per the pill rules in CONTEXT_PACK.md section 2 and 00_SHARED_CORE.md section 3. A figure marked confidence:unverified below is a best-known estimate that could not be confirmed against a live source this build; scout should not upgrade its pill past Estimate and should re-verify with a live lookup if the role's search specifically turns on that figure.

bls_oews_occupations.as_of: BLS OEWS (Occupational Employment and Wage Statistics) May 2025 national estimates, published Apr 2026
bls_oews_occupations.source: BLS Occupational Employment and Wage Statistics (api.bls.gov / bls.gov/oes), wage percentiles cross-checked via O*NET OnLine national wage tables (onetonline.org, sourced from the same BLS OEWS release)
bls_oews_occupations.note: Employment counts drawn from the BLS OEWS May 2025 national news-release table. Eight rows below have an employment figure that could not be independently confirmed this build (extraction ambiguity on a secondary table pull); those carry confidence:unverified on the employment field only, wage data on the same rows is independently sourced and considered reliable.

acs_metro_housing.source: Census Bureau QuickFacts, ACS 5-year tables B19013 (median household income), B25003 (owner-occupied rate), B25077 (median home value)
acs_metro_housing.note: Figures are the principal city's ACS numbers, used as a metro proxy per CONTEXT_PACK.md pack-research metros schema (relocation propensity, ownership, housing). A city figure understates a full CBSA/metro figure for dense core cities with large suburban homeowner rings (e.g. San Francisco city 38.2% ownership vs. the broader Bay Area metro, which runs well above 50%); scout should note this when a search's geography is metro-wide rather than core-city. Four metros below (Washington DC, Nashville, Salt Lake City, Minneapolis) could not be freshly confirmed this build; their figures are best-known estimates, confidence:unverified.
